findings.title: Harvests on the 'To' date are left out of the stats
findings.steps: Sign in. Open /stats?from=2026-07-15&to=2026-07-15 (there is a Tomato harvest of 450 g on 2026-07-15), or call GET /api/stats/harvests?from=2026-07-01&to=2026-07-20 (Courgette 1200 g was harvested on 2026-07-20).
findings.expected: The range includes both ends: 1 harvest of 450 g for 15 Jul, and Courgette 1200 g counted in 1–20 Jul.
findings.actual: The 15 Jul range returns 0 harvests and the page shows 'No harvests in this range'. The 1–20 Jul range shows only Tomato 450 g and leaves out the Courgette harvest from 20 Jul. Both queries use `harvested_on < to` where they should use `<=`.
findings.evidence: API returned {"plants":[],"harvest_count":0} for from=to=2026-07-15. The SSR page showed '0 harvests from 15 Jul 2026 to 15 Jul 2026' and 'No harvests in this range'. For 1–20 Jul total_grams was 450.

findings.title: Default range and dashboard 'Top plant this year' leave out 31 December
findings.steps: Log a harvest dated 31 Dec of the current year (possible once that date arrives), then look at the dashboard top plant and at /stats with the default range.
findings.expected: A harvest on 31 Dec counts toward this year's totals and the best plant.
findings.actual: top_plants() uses `< year_end` (12-31), so 31 Dec harvests are dropped. The dashboard used BETWEEN before this change, so this is a regression. It can also make the top plant disagree with harvest_grams_year, which still uses BETWEEN.
findings.evidence: Code: routers/stats.py top_plants uses `h.harvested_on < ?` with year_bounds() end = 12-31. dashboard.py now calls it in place of the old BETWEEN query.

findings.title: Stats error state has no retry
findings.steps: Open /stats while the API is down or returns 5xx.
findings.expected: An error message with a Retry button that refetches without reloading the page.
findings.actual: Only an AlertMessage is shown. There is no retry control, and the only way to retry is to change a date or reload the page.
findings.evidence: stats.vue renders <AlertMessage v-if="statsError"> with no button and does not use the refresh() returned by useApiFetch.

findings.title: Stats request has no timeout
findings.steps: Make the API hang (slow or stalled response) and open /stats.
findings.expected: The request fails after 10 seconds with a visible error.
findings.actual: useApiFetch/$fetch.create sets no timeout, so 'Loading stats…' can stay on screen forever.
findings.evidence: composables/useApi.ts has no timeout option. stats.vue passes none either.

findings.title: Bad date in the URL shows a raw technical validation message
findings.steps: Open /stats?from=2026-02-30 (it matches the page's regex but is not a real date).
findings.expected: A friendly reason, or a fallback to the default date.
findings.actual: The page shows the raw API message, roughly 'Query.from: Input should be a valid date or datetime, day value is outside expected range'.
findings.evidence: The API returns 422 with loc [query, from]. apiErrorMessage only strips 'body' from loc, not 'query'. queryDate() checks only the \d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} pattern.
